title: Furnace vs. Heat Pump... or both?! Know BEFORE you buy🔥🤯
summary: Denver HVAC contractor compares heat pumps and furnaces on climate, operating cost, ownership time, install cost and comfort, and recommends dual-fuel systems for cold climates.

assertions.quote: you have to look at the cost of natural gas in your area versus the cost of electricity
a very cold climate and very cheap natural gas prices it is almost always more efficient to run a high efficiency furnace
it has been rare to see scenarios where heat pumps are cheaper to run than furnaces
these are an excellent choice in climates like Colorado
if you have a surplus of solar energy you can run oftentimes run your heat pump for free
you need to upgrade your entire electrical panel

verdicts.note: Panel, service wire, transformer and pole upgrades are estimated at $2,000-$30,000; only 50-60% of homes already have panels above 150 amps.
RMI notes that many homes need additional electrical work to accommodate heat pumps.
Edwards lists electrical panel and other home upgrades among the upfront costs that can block heat pump adoption.

LBNL: electrification projects are often burdened by panel upgrades where amperage is insufficient; a typical 200 A panel upgrade costs $1,954, plus dedicated circuits, and many homes with 50- or 100-amp service cannot support the new loads.
Across 21 installs, 38% needed a new panel, 24% a service line upgrade and 90% new breakers for auxiliary heat; electrical upgrades alone cost $3,750-$8,970 in labour and materials.
The model adds an electrical panel upgrade cost (set at $3,400 in Table 2) for 1940 and 1980 homes where one is likely needed, including all heat-pump-with-electric-backup scenarios.

assertions.quote: you will have a long enough Break Even period to recoup these costs

verdicts.note: Savings accrue yearly, so a short ownership period may not recover a premium unless it is reflected in the sale price.

assertions.quote: if you're in a moderate climate a heat pump will be able to keep up year-round without breaking the bank

verdicts.note: Mild (mixed and coastal) climates have the greatest heat pump potential, and any beneficial gas replacement is in hot or mild climates; cold climates see the smallest benefit.
Homes with positive NPV from minimum-efficiency heat pumps include most gas homes with central AC in warmer climates.
Edwards' counties where heat pumps cut bills are warmer (mean HDD 3,016 versus 6,132 where they cost more), and heat pump use falls as heating degree days rise.
In mild Houston, RMI's heat pumps save over $3,500 in new construction and over $2,000 when the AC is replaced too, but gas stays cheaper for a plain furnace retrofit.

In relatively temperate Vancouver and Halifax (and cheap-electricity Montreal), heat pumps beat gas heating with AC in nearly all cases even with high equipment cost, high electricity and low gas prices.

assertions.quote: the cheapest option will always be swapping your existing unit with a like for light replacement

verdicts.note: Switching system types adds gas lines, circuits or ductwork changes, so like-for-like swaps usually cost least upfront.

Efficient heat pumps cost far more than like-for-like replacement, but a minimum-efficiency heat pump averaged $9,000 versus $11,000 for like-for-like furnace plus AC in cold-climate ducted homes with central AC.

assertions.quote: most high efficiency heat pumps are efficient down to as low as 0 to 10 degrees Fahrenheit
inverter heat pumps have and modulating furnaces take the cake in this category because they are very quiet

verdicts.note: Two to four of 7-17 respondents per season reported noise, mostly louder indoor airflow than their furnace plus a vibration and a bad bearing, but noise never affected overall satisfaction.
